newsitem.title: USA: Best Buy, three other retailers reach deal on ads.
newsitem.headline: Best Buy, three other retailers reach deal on ads.

text.p: Consumer electronics retailer Best Buy Co. Inc. and three other chains reached a deal Monday with 12 states that sets new standards for advertisements for "zero-interest" purchase programs.

Minneapolis-based Best Buy and the three other retailers, including Montgomery Ward & Co., CompUSA Inc. and Tandy Corp., together agreed to pay $925,000 to cover attorney fees and investigation costs.
Texas Attorney General Dan Morales said the investigation centered on advertisements offering consumers "no payments, no interest for one year" on purchases.

Under the agreement, the retailers have agreed to make it clear in advertisements that consumers are required to make minimum payments covering the purchase price of the product during the timeframe set by the financing contracts.
The retailers also must inform consumers that if they do not meet minimum payments when due, they are liable for interest accrued from the purchase date.
In addition to Texas, Arkansas, California, Florida, Iowa, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New Mexico, Tennessee, Vermont, Washington and Wisconsin were involved in the agreement.
While no lawsuit was filed, the deal is enforceable, Texas Attorney General Morales said. He said he hoped other retailers should follow the standards.
